verdict.rationale: Groq's batch API lets users submit workloads that run asynchronously in the background (24h–7 day windows) with no impact on standard rate limits, and its tool-use/MCP support enables autonomous agentic action-taking, which together partially satisfy the 'runs autonomously in the background' story. However there's no evidence of a scheduler, trigger system, or persistent agent runtime — users must build orchestration themselves. Missing for 10: scheduled/cron-style automation, persistent background agent execution, first-party workflow/automation builder, and independent evidence of hands-on automation use.
